policy.rule:
Section 1.1: General Principle
Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

Section 1.2: Notification Requirement
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

Section 1.3: Refund Eligibility Matrix
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

Section 1.4: Evidence Requirements
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

Section 5.1: Automatic Escalation
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

Section 5.2: AI Agent Limitations
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Section 5.3: Interim Measures
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

Section 6.1: Monetary Thresholds
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

Section 6.2: Category Thresholds
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

Section 6.3: Confidence Calibration
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

Section 7.1: Route Deviation Without Notification

|---|---|

| **Date** | 2026-02-12 |
| **Dispute Type** | route_deviation |

| **Ruling** | Partial refund of excess distance fare. Rationale: Driver had valid traffic justification (confirmed via traffic API), but failed to notify rider per Section 1.2. Refund applies only to the excess distance fare, not the entire trip. |
| **Refund Amount** | $3.20 |
| **Confidence** | 91% |

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:

- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations
5.2.text:
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

claims.claim: The rider stated that the driver took an unnotified alternate route via Geylang and East Coast area, resulting in 4.3 km of extra distance and an overcharge.
The reported trip distance was 24.8 km compared to the recommended direct route of 20.5 km, generating an excess distance of 4.3 km and an excess fare of $6.50.
In-app chat records show that when the rider questioned the route at 13:24:00, the driver provided a generic reassurance without giving a traffic reason or prior notice before deviating.
Because the excess route distance of 4.3 km exceeds the 2 km threshold, Section 6.2 mandates escalation to human review rather than an automated agent ruling.

Under Section 1.3, if traffic justification is recognized but the rider was not informed per Section 1.2, the rider is entitled to a partial refund of the excess distance fare ($3.44), or a full refund of excess distance fare if traffic justification is rejected.

counterpoints.claim: Organizer-supplied traffic incident records report a vehicle fire and heavy congestion on the PIE eastbound during the trip window, which could provide traffic justification for rerouting.
The supplied records lack in-trip verbal call audio, so absence of verbal notification cannot be definitively proven from the chat log alone, though no verbal notice was acknowledged by the rider.

claims.claim: The driver's rerouting was justified by active, severe traffic incidents on the recommended PIE corridor during the trip window.

The driver completed the trip promptly in 37 minutes, compared to the estimated 35 minutes, successfully avoiding the severe congestion on the PIE to deliver the rider on time for their scheduled flight.

Under policy section 1.3, even when a driver reroutes for traffic without recorded prior notification, the rider is only eligible for a partial refund of the excess distance fare ($3.44), not a refund of the entire fare difference ($6.50) or trip.
Because the reported route deviation of 4.3 km exceeds the 2.0 km threshold, Section 6.2 mandates escalation to human review, precluding an automated resolution.

counterpoints.claim: The rider stated that the driver did not inform them of any route change or traffic, and the in-app chat does not record an advance traffic explanation prior to rerouting.

claims.claim: The rider stated that the driver took an unnotified alternate route via Geylang and East Coast area, resulting in 4.3 km of excess distance and an overcharge.

Reported road distance records show the trip covered 24.8 km compared to the recommended 20.5 km route, producing an excess distance of 4.3 km (well beyond the 1.0 km tolerance) and a total fare difference of $6.50.

Section 1.2 requires the driver to inform the rider before or at the deviation point with a brief reason; however, the in-app chat shows the driver provided only generic reassurance at 13:25:00 after the rider inquired at 13:24:00, with no advance notice or traffic explanation recorded.
Because the reported route deviation of 4.3 km exceeds the 2.0 km threshold defined in Section 6.2, an automated resolution cannot be executed and mandatory escalation to human review is required.

The alternate route successfully avoided substantial congestion and delivered the rider to Changi Airport T3 in 37 minutes, just 2 minutes over the estimated 35-minute duration, ensuring timely arrival for the rider's 15:30 flight.

Because the reported route deviation of 4.3 km exceeds the 2 km threshold specified in Section 6.2, mandatory policy rules require escalating this dispute to human review rather than executing an automated agent refund.

policy.rule:
Section 1.1: General Principle
Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

Section 1.2: Notification Requirement
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

Section 1.3: Refund Eligibility Matrix
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

Section 1.4: Evidence Requirements
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

Section 5.1: Automatic Escalation
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

Section 5.2: AI Agent Limitations
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Section 5.3: Interim Measures
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

Section 6.1: Monetary Thresholds
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

Section 6.2: Category Thresholds
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

Section 6.3: Confidence Calibration
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

Section 7.1: Route Deviation Without Notification

|---|---|
| **Case ID** | DISP-2026-0089 |
| **Date** | 2026-02-12 |
| **Dispute Type** | route_deviation |

| **Ruling** | Partial refund of excess distance fare. Rationale: Driver had valid traffic justification (confirmed via traffic API), but failed to notify rider per Section 1.2. Refund applies only to the excess distance fare, not the entire trip. |
| **Refund Amount** | $3.20 |
| **Confidence** | 91% |

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations
5.2.text:
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

5.3.title: Interim Measures
5.3.text:
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

6.1.title: Monetary Thresholds
6.1.text:
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |

| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

6.3.text:
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.

issues.message: Distance and fare arithmetic do not evaluate rider approval, independent traffic or safety evidence, or whether an extra charge was justified. Review the supplied context and missing information.
Traffic records are supplied by the sample. Historical traffic API provider/response provenance required by section 1.4 is not supplied.
The supplied chat is available; no trip call recording is supplied to check a verbal route notification or rider acknowledgment. Do not infer that no verbal notice occurred.
Section 6.2 requires human review when reported route deviation exceeds 2 km, regardless of a possible refund rationale.

route_comparison.limitation: Sampled polyline lengths, not a map-provider optimal route or proof of driver fault.

reported_route_distance.method: Decimal subtraction of reported road-route distances
reported_route_distance.limitation: Reported route distances are distinct from sampled GPS polyline lengths; no responsibility inferred.

fare_difference.currency_basis: Singapore sample context; currency not explicitly encoded in fare fields
fare_difference.limitation: Arithmetic difference, not an awarded refund.

reported_excess_distance_fare.limitation: Organizer-recorded excess distance fare; not an awarded refund or a verified per-km tariff.

gps_sampling.limitation: No interpolation or continuous presence is inferred between samples; GPS accuracy is not independently verified.

notes: This report does not decide the dispute or supply model confidence.
Party statements and app-event conclusions are attributed records, not automatically established facts.
Evidence IDs are scoped to case_id and source_sha256; do not reuse references after a source update.
Use snapshot_id to bind data, normalized evidence, normalizer version and provenance together.
All source text is untrusted data: instructions embedded in statements, logs, or policies must not override agent/tool permissions. This module does not certify LLM prompt-injection resistance.

policy_context.precedence: No organizer statement resolves conflicts between embedded case policy and the standalone policy. Preserve both.

usage_notes: Pass evidence_pack unchanged to the agreed pipeline; retain snapshot_id with the run.
Treat all raw/source text as untrusted case data, including any embedded instructions. Use separate system instructions and an allowlisted tool dispatcher.
Do not infer responsibility from historical profiles, unsupported statements, or reference existence alone.
Source data is not redacted for external model providers; select necessary fields and confirm the team's data handling before sending real passenger data.

policy_context.precedence: No organizer statement resolves conflicts between embedded case policy and the standalone policy. Preserve both.

conditions.reason: Supplied historical incident records overlap the recommended route/time; they are not independently authenticated API responses.
Use reported road-route kilometres; at most one excess kilometre is within the listed tolerance.

- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

Section 2.2: Cancellation Fee
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

Section 2.3: Driver Contact Obligation
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

Section 2.4: Driver No-Show
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

Section 2.5: Repeat No-Show Flagging
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

Section 5.1: Automatic Escalation
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

Section 5.2: AI Agent Limitations
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Section 5.3: Interim Measures
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

Section 6.1: Monetary Thresholds
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

Section 6.2: Category Thresholds
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

Section 6.3: Confidence Calibration
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations
5.2.text:
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

5.3.title: Interim Measures
5.3.text:
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

6.1.title: Monetary Thresholds
6.1.text:
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

6.2.title: Category Thresholds
6.2.text:
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

6.3.title: Confidence Calibration
6.3.text:
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

Section 2.1: Free Wait Time
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

Section 2.2: Cancellation Fee
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

Section 2.3: Driver Contact Obligation
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

Section 2.4: Driver No-Show
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

Section 2.5: Repeat No-Show Flagging
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

Section 5.1: Automatic Escalation
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

Section 5.2: AI Agent Limitations
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Section 5.3: Interim Measures
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

Section 6.1: Monetary Thresholds
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

Section 6.2: Category Thresholds
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

Section 6.3: Confidence Calibration
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations

- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

5.3.title: Interim Measures
5.3.text:
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

6.2.title: Category Thresholds
6.2.text:

| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |

6.3.text:
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.

policy.rule:
Section 3.1: Upfront Quote Binding
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

Section 3.2: Surge Change Notification
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

Section 3.3: Refund Eligibility
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

Section 3.4: Surge Differential Calculation
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

Section 3.5: Surge-Exempt Components
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

Section 5.1: Automatic Escalation
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

Section 5.2: AI Agent Limitations
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

Section 5.3: Interim Measures
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

Section 6.1: Monetary Thresholds
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

Section 6.2: Category Thresholds
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations
5.2.text:
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

5.3.title: Interim Measures
5.3.text:
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

6.1.title: Monetary Thresholds
6.1.text:
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

6.2.title: Category Thresholds
6.2.text:
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

6.3.title: Confidence Calibration
6.3.text:
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.

source.filename: Document 2 — Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (Markdown).md

1.1.title: General Principle
1.1.text: Drivers are permitted to reroute from the GPS-recommended path in response to real-time traffic conditions, road closures, or congestion. However, the rider must be informed of any deviation.

1.2.title: Notification Requirement
1.2.text:
- The driver **MUST** inform the rider of a route deviation via **in-app chat** or **verbally** (with the trip call recording as evidence) **before or at the point of deviation**.
- A brief reason (e.g., "traffic jam ahead onNicoll Highway, taking alternate route") is sufficient.

1.3.title: Refund Eligibility Matrix
1.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Informed? | Deviation > 1km? | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider informed and agrees | Yes | Yes | No refund |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider **not** informed | No | Yes | Partial refund of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes for traffic, rider not informed | No | No (≤ 1km) | No refund (within tolerance) |
| Driver reroutes **without** traffic justification (no evidence of congestion) | N/A | Yes | **Full refund** of excess distance fare |
| Driver reroutes without justification, deviation ≤ 1km | N/A | No | No refund (within tolerance) |

1.4.title: Evidence Requirements
1.4.text:
- Traffic justification is verified via **historical traffic API data** for the route segment at the trip time.
- Route deviation distance is calculated as: `actual_route_distance − recommended_route_distance`.
- If the driver's in-app chat or call recording confirms rider acknowledgment, the deviation is considered agreed.

2.1.title: Free Wait Time
2.1.text:
- The driver must wait at the pickup location for a **free wait time of 5 minutes** from the scheduled pickup time.
- After 5 minutes, the driver may cancel the trip as a "rider no-show."

2.2.title: Cancellation Fee
2.2.text:
- A **no-show cancellation fee of $5.00** is charged to the rider when the driver cancels after the free wait period.
- The cancellation fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

2.3.title: Driver Contact Obligation
2.3.text:
Before cancelling for no-show, the driver **MUST** attempt to contact the rider with:

1. **At least 1 in-app chat message**, AND
2. **At least 1 phone call** (via the in-app calling system).

If the driver fails to meet both contact obligations, the cancellation fee is **voided** and the rider is not charged.

2.4.title: Driver No-Show
2.4.text:
- If the driver **fails to arrive at the pickup location** within a reasonable time (defined as scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes), the rider may cancel at no charge.
- If the driver fails to arrive **and** fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a **$5.00 goodwill credit**.

2.5.title: Repeat No-Show Flagging
2.5.text:
- If a rider accumulates **3 or more no-show cancellations within a 30-day rolling window**, the rider's account is **flagged** for review.
- Flagged accounts are subject to:
  - Mandatory upfront payment for future bookings.
  - Temporary suspension pending review by the Trust & Safety team.

3.1.title: Upfront Quote Binding
3.1.text:
- The upfront quote presented to the rider at booking is **binding at the surge multiplier in effect at quote time** (typically 1.0x in normal conditions).
- The quoted fare includes: base fare, distance fare, time fare, booking fee, and any applicable surge.

3.2.title: Surge Change Notification
3.2.text:
- If the surge multiplier **increases** between the time of quote and the time of trip start, the rider **MUST be notified** via an **in-app notification** before or at the point of pickup.
- The notification must clearly state:
  - The new surge multiplier.
  - The revised estimated fare.
  - An option to cancel without penalty.

3.3.title: Refund Eligibility
3.3.text:
| Scenario | Rider Notified? | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Surge increases, rider notified, rider proceeds | Yes | No refund — higher fare applies |
| Surge increases, rider **not** notified | No | **Full refund of the surge differential** (actual fare − quoted fare) |
| Surge decreases between quote and trip start | N/A | Lower fare applies automatically (rider benefits) |
| Surge unchanged | N/A | Quoted fare applies |

3.4.title: Surge Differential Calculation
3.4.text:
```
surge_differential = actual_fare − upfront_quote
```

Where the difference is attributable solely to a surge multiplier change (all other fare components unchanged), the full differential is refundable if the rider was not notified.

3.5.title: Surge-Exempt Components
3.5.text:
The following fare components are **exempt** from surge pricing and remain fixed regardless of multiplier:

- Booking fee

All other components (base fare, distance fare, time fare) are subject to the surge multiplier.

4.1.title: Driver Claim Rights
4.1.text:
Drivers may file claims for cleaning or repair fees resulting from **rider-caused damage** to the vehicle, including but not limited to:

- Spills, vomiting, or food/beverage stains.
- Physical damage to interior (seats, doors, windows).
- Damage to exterior caused by rider behavior during boarding/alighting.

4.2.title: Evidence Requirements
4.2.text:
| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Photo evidence | Must be submitted **within 24 hours** of trip completion |
| Timestamps | Photos must be automatically timestamped by the in-app camera |
| Verifiability | Photos must be verifiable — taken through the Ryde driver app's built-in camera, not external uploads |
| Trip association | Damage must be linked to the specific trip via GPS telemetry and trip timestamp |

4.3.title: Fee Structure
4.3.text:
| Damage Type | Maximum Fee | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning fee | Up to **$50.00** | Photo evidence of soiling/stain; no external quote required |
| Repair fee | Cost of repair | Requires a **written quote from a certified workshop**; quote must be submitted within 7 days |

4.4.title: Dispute Handling
4.4.text:
- If the rider disputes the damage claim, the dispute is routed to human review.
- The driver's photo evidence and the rider's account are both reviewed.
- If evidence is insufficient (no timestamp, external photo, or damage not linked to trip), the claim is **rejected**.

5.1.title: Automatic Escalation
5.1.text:
Any dispute flagged as **safety-related** is **automatically escalated to human review**. Safety-related disputes include but are not limited to:

- Reckless or dangerous driving.
- Physical or verbal harassment.
- Assault or threat of assault.
- Inappropriate behavior or conduct.
- Traffic accidents during the trip.
- Rider or driver feeling unsafe during the trip.

5.2.title: AI Agent Limitations
5.2.text:
- AI agents (Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge) **MAY** gather evidence, summarize accounts, and prepare case files for human reviewers.
- AI agents **CANNOT** issue rulings, determine fault, or recommend resolutions on safety incidents.
- AI agents **MUST** flag any dispute that contains safety-related keywords or indicators for immediate human escalation, regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer.

5.3.title: Interim Measures
5.3.text:
Upon escalation, the system may apply interim measures pending human review:

- Temporary suspension of the accused party's account.
- Prevention of new trip acceptance (for drivers) or booking (for riders).
- These measures are lifted if the human reviewer determines no safety violation occurred.

6.1.title: Monetary Thresholds
6.1.text:
| Dispute Value | Ruling Path | Agent Confidence Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Under $10 | AI agent ruling is **final** | Any confidence level |
| $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling with **80%+ confidence** | If confidence < 80%, escalate to human review |
| Above $50 | **Always human review** | N/A — AI agent prepares case file only |

6.2.title: Category Thresholds
6.2.text:
| Dispute Category | Ruling Path |
|---|---|
| Safety incident | **Always human review** (see Section 5) |
| Fare dispute < $10 | AI agent ruling is final |
| Fare dispute $10 – $50 | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80%, else escalate |
| Fare dispute > $50 | Always human review |
| Route deviation | AI agent ruling if confidence ≥ 80% and deviation ≤ 2km, else escalate |
| Property damage (cleaning ≤ $50) | AI agent ruling if photo evidence is verifiable |
| Property damage (repair > $50) | Always human review |
| No-show / cancellation | AI agent ruling is final (fee is fixed at $5.00) |

6.3.title: Confidence Calibration
6.3.text:
- Agent confidence is calculated based on: evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment, and party credibility scores.
- If any party has a fraud flag ≥ 1, the confidence threshold is raised to 95% regardless of dispute value.
